title: The grapes
subtitle: Garnacha and Cariñena
objectives: Explain the role of old vines

steps.title: Old natives
steps.body: Garnacha and Cariñena, Carignan, are Priorat's traditional grapes, many from old bush vines over 50 or 80 years old. Garnacha gives ripe red fruit, spice and warmth; Cariñena gives acidity, colour and structure. Together, on llicorella, they make powerful, dark, mineral reds, often 14.5 to 15.5% alcohol.

steps.title: International partners
steps.body: The 1989 pioneers also planted Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Merlot, adding structure and colour to blends. Today many producers focus on the native grapes, especially old Garnacha and Cariñena, and on single vineyards. Whites, from Garnacha Blanca and Macabeo, are rare.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.
steps.explanation: Old natives lead; international grapes support.

steps.body: Neighbouring Montsant, which surrounds Priorat, makes similar Garnacha and Cariñena blends at lower prices, on more varied soils.

steps.prompt: What do old vines give Priorat's wines?
steps.explanation: Old vines on llicorella give very low yields and concentration.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Garnacha and Cariñena are Priorat's traditional grapes
Old bush vines give concentrated, mineral wines
